mission_09: The Listen, Attend and Spell (LAS) model is a pioneering end-to-end neural speech recognition architecture that directly maps audio features to character sequences without intermediate phoneme representations or alignment supervision. The model consists of three components: a listener (encoder) that processes the audio sequence into high-level representations, an attention mechanism that dynamically focuses on relevant parts of the encoded audio, and a speller (decoder) that generates the output character sequence autoregressively. The listener uses a bidirectional LSTM-style encoder that processes the audio in both forward and backward directions, capturing context from past and future frames. The Bahdanau attention mechanism computes a context vector for each decoder step by scoring the relevance of each encoder position to the current decoder state, using a learned alignment function. The speller is an autoregressive RNN that generates one character at a time, conditioned on the previous character embedding, the attention context, and its hidden state. The model is trained end-to-end using cross-entropy loss, with gradients flowing through the attention mechanism to jointly optimize all components. In this mission, you will implement the LAS encoder, Bahdanau attention, the decoder step, autoregressive transcription, and loss computation.
